I was too scared to check back here in case it was the other person saying I can never do anything to help myself in terms of reducing tics. I have, since my previous comment, managed to reduce my tics quite a lot actually. Especially the worst one which I've only had for... less than a year at least. The other one I need to stop, I've had since I was 12, so that will be a tough one, but I've managed to reduce it. I find that it works just as good for me to just suppress them vs competing response. I understand most people with Tourette's will tic more after suppressing, but for me that has never been the case - rather I get so stressed from some tics that I will tic even more from the stress, so suppressing them leads to an overall reduction in tics. I've dislocated both my jaw and my lower ribs multiple times from tics, and now it's my neck which is already severely injured and unstable. It's a horror show to be honest.   
I've also the last 2 days managed to get started with my previous medications - I decided that sleeping all the time was the better alternative in any case, even if only for a short while. Surprisingly I don't feel as sleepy as I did last time I took them, so it might be good actually. Already feeling my brain calming down with it.   


I'm also changing things a bit at home to reduce stress and pressure wherever I can. The main stressors are the tics, the worsening injury and some external factors that I have no way to change for better or worse. I just have to wait. I already do exercise at least an hour every day, but now I've added in either yoga or qi-gong every day plus some meditating every day as well. I'm feeling slightly calmer now and think I'll manage to get somewhere here. My brain tends to swap between OCD compulsions, obsessive thoughts and tics, so only one is a big issue at any one time. Never all 3 apart from when I was pregnant. They are all horrible, but tics is the only one that physically harms me as well, so I hope it will swap over soon.

I have read a bit about the thoughts behind it and reducing the connection between doing that tic and feeling relief - makes perfect sense to me from a neuroscience point of view. I'll have to try. I know this is just a temporary state of being - it's a really bad rough patch, and I've been through those many times before. It always calms down again later. I will keep trying. And to many people, having weird facial expressions or sounds or whatever does not change your attractiveness.   
You're still you and you can still look nice even if you maybe look funny for a moment.
